source.title: Class-wise Activation Unravelling the Engima of Deep Double Descent

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper describes its model-wise experiments as a replication of prior double-descent work and sweeps neural-network width while measuring test error, although it uses its own architectures and datasets.
record.gate_note: The paper tests test-error curves across model widths and reports a class-wise activation-richness measure against those curves. Epoch-wise and sample-wise curves are not swept. Similarity, k-NN, sparsity, and architecture-comparison results are not separate rows here because they do not measure the test-error shapes or the effective-complexity measure named in the tested versions.
record.test_reason: Chapter 2 sweeps network width with no regularization and plots test error under 0/10/20% added label noise. It is framed as a replication of Belkin et al.'s two-layer FCNN on MNIST (N=4000) and Nakkiran et al.'s CNN and ResNet18 on CIFAR-10. Same method and measure as the originals, so it tests V1 and the label-noise part of V6. The class-wise 'richness' measure is the paper's own construct; it is not tested as a predictor of peak location.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with corrections. The authors reproduce model-wise double descent across FCNN, CNN and ResNet18, but say the peak is not universal: it is absent for noise-free FCNN/MNIST, which they attribute to task complexity and label noise. They report that richness shows 'surprisingly good alignment' with double descent in most cases, while its relation to true complexity is unclear. They also conclude that over-parameterized nets isolate noisy samples (FCNN), weakly for CNNs and in reverse for ResNets, and that overfitting persists across architectures of greater expressive capacity.
record.recipe_differences: Width sweeps and test-error measurements closely follow prior double-descent experiments, but use two-layer FCNNs on MNIST and CNN/ResNet18 families on CIFAR-10, with the paper's own training setup and width ranges.
record.method_sensitivity: The curve varies with architecture, dataset, and explicit label-noise ratio. For FCNNs on MNIST, the noise-free curve is monotone while added noise produces a peak. Added noise also shifts the reported CIFAR-10 CNN interpolation threshold and peak rightward.

fits_no_version.finding: Class-wise activation 'richness', a sub-sampled Rademacher-style estimate, tracks the test-loss double-descent shape for FCNNs and CNNs. It peaks slightly after the interpolation threshold and falls in the over-parameterized regime. It is absent for ResNet18 at p=0 and weak at 10% and 20% noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An activation-based complexity measure itself shows a double-descent shape across width that mirrors test loss.

fits_no_version.finding: k-NN accuracy P of noisy-labelled training points against clean neighbours tracks test accuracy for FCNNs and weakly for CNNs. For ResNet18 it reverses, dropping to 0 past the threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-parameterized networks isolate noisy-labelled samples among clean representations, depending on architecture.

record.problems: Test-error and richness values are presented in figures without numerical tables or reported uncertainty. The paper reports averaging repeated experiments but does not state the repetition count. The proposed richness estimate is described as rough, and the paper says its relation to true model complexity is unclear. The paper also gives differing descriptions of the data used for richness estimation: the method section specifies unseen test images, while the results section refers to the training dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying test-error or activation-richness results were omitted. The paper's other reported measures (CAM similarities, k-NN noisy-sample accuracy, activation sparsity, NDCG, and the depth-versus-width experiment) do not directly measure the behaviors named by the tested versions.

untested.parts: All of it: there is no sweep over training epochs.
All of it: there is no sweep over training-sample size.
Non-deep model classes: only FCNN, CNN and ResNet18 are tested.
All of it: EMC is not computed, and the paper's richness measure is not tested as a predictor of peak location.
Variance as the driver, multiple or triple peaks, and removal of the peak by optimally tuned regularization. No regularization is used at all.
All of it: complexity is never recounted as an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Test error vs width at high added noise (p=40%, 60%). The FCNN threshold shifts from k=20 to k=40, test accuracy falls about 30%, and the peak is more pronounced. At p=60% the k=1000 loss is comparable to the k=5 sweet spot. The CNN peak shifts rightward and error stays high even when over-parameterized.
x-axis is width k, not parameter count. Appendix A gives the monotone mapping, with ResNet18 having more parameters per k.

record.verdict_notes: This is an M.Eng thesis preprint; Chapters 2 and 5 overlap with Gu et al. (ICLR 2024). All evidence is figures only, with no numbers or error bars, and the repetition count is not stated. The training lr formula for CNN/ResNet looks garbled ('1+[epoch*10]'). The text is inconsistent about whether richness uses test or training data. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: No settings beyond the stated image-classification architectures, datasets, and width ranges.
No test-error sweep over training epochs; epochs are training durations, not the varied axis.
Tests several deep-network architectures, not a sweep across model classes including non-deep models.

Tests the paper's activation-richness estimate against model-width results only; does not test whether one measure predicts peak location across epochs and sample size, or whether it is the same as EMC.
Varies explicit label-noise ratios and reports peak changes. Does not test multiple or triple peaks, variance as a cause, or optimally tuned regularization.
Does not recount complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that transforms the curve into an ordinary U-shape.
